When both factors are whole numbers, then:

$\blueE{\text{factor}} \times \blueE{\text{factor}} = \maroonD{\text{multiple}}$

###Multiples of $7$

$\begin{align}
\blueE{7} \times \blueE{1} &= \maroonD{7}\\\\
\blueE{7} \times \blueE{2} &= \maroonD{14}\\\\
\blueE{7} \times \blueE{3} &= \maroonD{21}\\\\
\blueE{7} \times \blueE{4} &= \maroonD{28}\\\\
\blueE{7} \times \blueE{5} &= \maroonD{35}\\\\
\blueE{7} \times \blueE{6} &= \maroonD{42}\\\\
\blueE{7} \times \blueE{7} &= \maroonD{49}\\\\
\blueE{7} \times \blueE{8} &= \maroonD{56}\\\\
\blueE{7} \times \blueE{9} &= \maroonD{63}\\\\
\blueE{7} \times \blueE{10} &= \maroonD{70}\\\\
\blueE{7} \times \blueE{11} &= \maroonD{77}\\\\
\blueE{7} \times \blueE{12} &= \maroonD{84}\\\\
\blueE{7} \times \blueE{13} &= \maroonD{91}\\\\
\blueE{7} \times \blueE{14} &= \maroonD{98}
\end{align}$

All of the shaded numbers in the table are multiples of $\blueE{7}$. Every multiple of $7$ between $1$ and $100$ is shaded.
The shaded numbers on the hundred chart are only the multiples of $7$.
